summary: Add a board layer to an existing csolution by asking for the few open decisions, then build it
triggers: add or author a board layer
would rather be asked than hand over every parameter up front
unmapped: DFP and BSP packs of the board
verification: Read the ✅/❌ line that ends the result; a build still running when the call's wait ends returns status `running`, and `cmsis_action` with `action: 'status'` waits for it.
Verify the load-bearing ones on the target later (write via the debugger, read back).
Show the user the layer file set, the csolution diff, and the green build summary.
stop_conditions: If the tools are missing from your tool list, suggest the setting instead of asking.
Open in prose with the one open-ended question — **"Which board or device are you adding, and is there an on-board debug probe / VCP?"** — then resolve §2.
Everything after that is a small set of decisions: ask them with `AskUserQuestion`, **batched**, each with a recommended default derived from what you read in §0/§2.
A missing internal-flash FLM is a flashing blocker to raise **before** writing a line.
If a name is fuzzy or several candidates remain, that is the moment for one `AskUserQuestion` to disambiguate — with the resolved candidates as options.
**Tell the user to run the generator — you cannot do it for them.**
If the result says RTE or configuration files of the new target-type are missing, ask the user to run **CMSIS: Refresh (Reload Packs, Update RTE)** in VS Code, then build again.

extracted.title: A DFP with a configuration generator may ship no Device:Startup component
extracted.body: **Does the DFP ship startup, or a generator?** Check both: `grep -c 'Cgroup="Startup"' <DFP>.pdsc` and `grep -o '<generator id="[^"]*"' <DFP>.pdsc`. A DFP with a `<generator>` (STM32CubeMX, MCUXpresso Config Tools, Infineon Device Configurator, Microchip MCC, …) may ship **no classic `Device:Startup` component at all** — startup, `SystemInit`, clock and pin configuration exist only as generator output (components carrying `generator="<id>"`).

extracted.title: Enable only the I-cache during bring-up
extracted.body: During bring-up enable **I-cache only**; a write-back D-cache makes halted-mode debugger reads stale and poisons the very validation you are about to do.

extracted.title: Register read-back tells: wrong address or unclocked peripheral
extracted.body: Tells: reads-back-0 always → reserved/wrong address; several registers of one peripheral reading the **same** value → the peripheral is unclocked and the bus is echoing garbage. When the hardware disagrees with the manual, search the errata document before changing code.

extracted.title: RAM at 100% in the build summary
extracted.body: RAM at "100%" in the summary is usually the stack pinned at the region top by the template — read the map before panicking.

extracted.title: CMSIS pack root and automatic pack download
extracted.body: Pack root: `$CMSIS_PACK_ROOT` (default `~/.cache/arm/packs` on Linux and macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Arm\Packs` on Windows). Missing packs need no command from you: the CMSIS Solution extension downloads them when it loads the solution and when `cmsis_action build` runs (its setting `cmsis-csolution.downloadPacks`, on by default). `cpackget add Vendor::Pack` or `cbuild --packs` only when the user works from a terminal.
